title: AI marketing tools for small business: the free kit that is enough
excerpt: Most of the AI a small business needs is already inside Google Ads, Meta, Business Profile and Canva. What each free tool does, a weekly routine, and what to skip.

featuredImage.alt: A shopkeeper's hands on a Midnight MacBook Air on a Pune sweet shop counter, one app tile glowing violet

paragraphs: The best AI marketing tools for small business are mostly free, and the average shop owner has already logged into two of them this month. Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Google Business Profile and Search Console either run AI or feed it the data it needs. Add one writing assistant and Canva. That is the whole kit.

Paid subscriptions can wait. Below: what each free tool is good at, a weekly routine that takes about an hour, the paid tools a small business can safely ignore, and the point at which paying for help starts to make sense.

sections.heading: Key takeaways
points: Use the AI already built into Google Ads and Meta before buying anything. It comes with the ad spend.
Pick one general assistant and learn it properly. Three half-used subscriptions cost more time than they save.
Nothing AI writes goes live until a person has checked the price, the offer and every claim in it.
Walk away from any tool that promises leads without first asking how a lead will be counted.

sections.heading: What can AI do for my business?
paragraphs: For a small business, AI does three jobs well: it writes first drafts, it tests more ad versions than a person could, and it reads data quickly. It cannot pick the offer. Nor does it know which customers pay late, which festival week the shop gets busiest, or why the regulars keep coming back after the new place opened down the road.

Think of a sweet shop in Kothrud before Diwali. AI can draft twenty ad headlines in a minute, suggest which ones Google should rotate, and summarise last year's search terms so the owner knows people typed "dry fruit box" far more than "mithai hamper". Useful. The owner still decides the box sizes, the price and the delivery cut-off date.

That split holds for almost every business. Give AI the repetitive work. Keep judgement, offers and customer promises with a person, because a wrong promise in an ad is the owner's problem, never the software's.

sections.heading: Which AI marketing tools for small business are free?
paragraphs: Seven free tools cover nearly everything a small business needs. Some are AI themselves; the rest supply the data an assistant can read.
points: Google Ads: [Smart Bidding](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7065882) sets a bid for each auction, and a [responsive search ad](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7684791) takes up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions, then tests the combinations for you. Keyword Planner, inside the same account, shows search volumes and bid ranges at no cost.

Meta Ads Manager: [Advantage+ creative](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/297506218282224) can make small automatic changes to images, videos and text so each person sees the version most likely to work. Each enhancement can be switched off.
Google Business Profile: this is the listing people see on Maps. It costs nothing and is where a shop replies to reviews and gets the link or QR code that asks happy customers to review it.
Search Console: its performance report lists the searches that brought people to the website, with clicks and impressions, and exports to a spreadsheet.
Google Analytics 4: shows which pages and channels bring enquiries, so an assistant can be asked sensible questions about it.
ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: each has a free tier that drafts captions, ad copy, replies to reviews and product descriptions, and can read an exported report.
Canva: its AI features help with quick social posts and resized ad images. Some of them sit in the paid plan, so check what the free account includes before building a routine around one.

sections.heading: How can AI help small businesses every week?
paragraphs: AI helps most when it runs inside a fixed routine instead of whenever someone remembers. One hour on a Monday is enough for most shops, clinics and service businesses with a single location.
points: Download last week's search terms from Google Ads and ask the assistant to group them into relevant, irrelevant and new ideas. Add the irrelevant ones as negative keywords.
Export the Search Console queries for the last 28 days and ask which questions the website does not answer yet. That list becomes next month's pages and posts.
Ask for five new headlines and two new primary texts for the best ad, edit them for tone and facts, and add the best two to the campaign.
Reply to every new Google review in the shop's own voice. AI can draft the reply; a person should send it.
Plan the week's social posts in Canva from one photo shot in the shop, resized for Instagram and WhatsApp Status.

sections.heading: Which paid AI tools can a small business skip?
paragraphs: Most. A business spending a modest amount on ads gets very little from a tool that does what Google, Meta and a free assistant already do.

Some do harm. Tools that generate hundreds of near-identical blog pages risk breaking Google's [spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) on scaled content. Anything that posts reviews on a customer's behalf, invents them, or rewards people for posting them breaks Google's rules on fake engagement in its [review guidelines](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7035772), and a profile can lose reviews over it.

Be careful with auto-posting tools that publish AI captions without anyone reading them first. One wrong price or a festival greeting on the wrong day is enough to make a local brand look careless. The same goes for "AI lead generation" products that sell contact lists. Those people never asked to hear from the business.

sections.heading: Are free AI marketing tools enough, or should you pay?
paragraphs: Free tools are enough while the owner has an hour a week, one location and a simple offer, and while the ad spend is small enough that a slow week of learning does not hurt the month. Most small businesses start here, and many never need more software.

Paying makes sense in two cases. The first is when the time spent on marketing is costing sales, because the owner is writing captions instead of serving customers. The second is when ad spend has grown and small mistakes in tracking or bidding now cost real money every week. In both cases the gap is usually a person who knows the platforms well, so more software rarely fills it.
For a wider view of where AI fits across ads, SEO and creative, read [what AI marketing is and which parts move leads](/blog/what-is-ai-marketing).

faqs.a: They are tools that use machine learning or generative AI to write, design, target, bid or analyse. For a small business the most useful ones are the AI inside Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager, a general assistant such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, and Canva for quick creative.

faqs.q: Is ChatGPT enough for small business marketing?
faqs.a: It is enough for drafting captions, ad copy, review replies and reading exported reports. It cannot run ads, see live account data or know local prices, so every draft needs a person to check facts before it goes out. Claude and Gemini do the same jobs; pick the one you find easiest and stick with it.

faqs.q: Can AI write Google reviews for my business?
faqs.a: No. Reviews must come from real customers describing a real experience, and Google treats paid or incentivised reviews as fake content. AI can help a happy customer phrase what they want to say, and it can draft the owner's reply, but the review itself has to be theirs.

faqs.q: Will AI-written posts hurt my website's SEO?
faqs.a: Not because AI wrote them. Google says it rewards helpful content however it is made, in its guidance on [generative AI content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content). Thin, repetitive pages made only to rank are the problem, whoever writes them.

faqs.q: What is the first AI tool a small business should set up?
faqs.a: Conversion tracking in Google Ads and Meta, even though it is not an AI tool. Smart Bidding and Advantage+ learn from whatever is counted as a result, so without tracking they optimise for clicks. Once calls, forms and WhatsApp enquiries are counted, every other tool gets more useful.
